title: When the Alibi Turns
premise: Retired detective Paloma Villalobos receives a confession letter for a murder committed the day after the victim's funeral — a crime she realizes was pinned on a man already tried and acquitted decades ago, in a case whose file only she ever fully memorized. As she reopens the investigation from her failing bookshop, she discovers the confessor is someone inside the original case who has been watching her for years, feeding her clues to force her to relive her greatest failure. The killer's true target is not justice but control of the narrative: they intend to destroy the acquitted man's life a second time before a new trial begins. Paloma must stage an elaborate trap using her own memory as bait, ending with her confronting the killer in the bookshop's back room, where the confession letter was written all along.
about_author: Felix Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former court stenographer who spent twenty years transcribing testimony before turning to fiction. They write mysteries obsessed with what records remember and people forget.

chapters.title: Postmarked After
chapters.summary: Paloma Villalobos, closing up her struggling bookshop, finds a confession letter describing a murder that occurred the day after the funeral of Judge Emilio Sartorius. Her POV; the beat is cold dread wrapped in professional curiosity, as the letter quotes details never made public.

chapters.title: The File She Memorized
chapters.summary: Paloma digs out her private notes from the 1998 Sartorius case, the acquittal that ended her career. Third-person limited on Paloma; the emotional beat is shame resurfacing as she realizes the letter's author knows the file better than any investigator alive.

chapters.title: A Customer Who Buys Nothing
chapters.summary: A well-dressed stranger browses the shop for hours, asking oddly precise questions about true-crime titles. Paloma's POV; suspicion and unease build as she recognizes phrasing from the confession letter echoed back at her.

chapters.title: What the Widow Kept
chapters.summary: Paloma visits Sartorius's widow, Marisol, who reveals a second letter arrived before the first. Marisol's POV; grief curdles into fear as she admits she destroyed it — and that it named Paloma.

chapters.title: The Acquitted Man
chapters.summary: Paloma tracks down Tomás Iriarte, the man acquitted in '98, now living quietly under a changed name. His POV; relief shatters into terror when he learns someone is rebuilding the case against him ahead of a reopened trial.

chapters.title: Twenty-Six Years of Watching
chapters.summary: Paloma discovers surveillance photos of herself spanning two decades, tucked inside a hollowed book returned to her shop. Her POV; the beat is violation — the watcher has been a fixture of her whole retired life.

chapters.title: The Prosecutor's Regret
chapters.summary: Paloma confronts aging prosecutor Beatriz Ondiz, who confesses she suppressed evidence to win a conviction she knew was shaky. Beatriz's POV; guilt and self-justification war as she hints who else knew about the suppressed page.

chapters.title: Missing Page Nine
chapters.summary: Paloma reconstructs the missing evidence page from memory alone, realizing its contents point to a third party at the scene. Her POV; exhilaration turns to horror when she understands why the killer wants the trial restarted — to weaponize that page.

chapters.title: Dead Drop in the Stacks
chapters.summary: A second letter appears shelved inside a customer's special order, escalating the game. Paloma's POV; anger hardens into resolve as she decides to stop reacting and start hunting.

chapters.title: Marisol's Silence
chapters.summary: Paloma returns to find Marisol hospitalized after a staged break-in; the intruder took nothing but old photographs. Marisol's POV; helplessness and betrayal as she realizes her silence protected the wrong person for years.

chapters.title: The Apprentice Theory
chapters.summary: Paloma maps everyone with access to the original file and lands on a young clerk from '98, Néstor Aguirre, now a respected legal archivist. Her POV; the beat is reluctant certainty shadowed by doubt, because the theory fits too neatly.

chapters.title: Trial Date Set
chapters.summary: The state announces Iriarte's retrial, compressing Paloma's timeline to six weeks. Alternating POVs of Paloma and Iriarte; dread becomes urgency as both realize the killer engineered the timing itself.

chapters.title: Néstor Aguirre, Charming and Clean
chapters.summary: Paloma interviews Aguirre under the pretense of donating case materials to his archive. Dual-tension scene from her POV; his flawless answers feel rehearsed, yet one slip suggests he knows about page nine.

chapters.title: The Letter That Lies
chapters.summary: Forensic analysis shows the confession letters were written by two different hands — or one hand imitating two. Paloma's POV; the ground shifts as she questions whether the confessor and the killer are allies or enemies.

chapters.title: Iriarte Runs
chapters.summary: Panicked by a threatening note, Iriarte flees town, becoming a fugitive and handing the prosecution its narrative. His POV; desperation and self-loathing as he repeats the worst mistake of his life.

chapters.title: Ondiz Found Dead
chapters.summary: Prosecutor Ondiz dies in an apparent suicide, leaving a note quoting Paloma's own case notes verbatim. Paloma's POV; grief collapses into fury — the killer is erasing every witness to the original cover-up.

chapters.title: The Memory Trap
chapters.summary: Paloma devises her trap: she will leak a fabricated version of page nine containing a detail only the true killer would correct. Her POV; cold clarity and risk, gambling her reputation and safety on her own recall.

chapters.title: Bait Taken
chapters.summary: The corrected fabrication surfaces in an anonymous tip to prosecutors, confirming the killer's access and identity pattern. Paloma's POV; grim triumph shadowed by fear as the net closes on someone she once trusted.

chapters.title: The Back Room
chapters.summary: Paloma lures the killer to her bookshop after hours with the promise of the real page nine. Her POV; controlled terror as the confrontation begins and the mask drops — it is the quiet customer, Aguirre's protégé, acting under Aguirre's design.

chapters.title: Confession, Interrupted
chapters.summary: The killer monologues their motive — avenging a parent destroyed by the '98 cover-up — and moves to kill Paloma; she springs the recorded trap as police arrive. Climactic dual tension; the beat is survival bought at the edge of death.

chapters.title: What Survives the Record
chapters.summary: In the aftermath, Aguirre is arrested, the retrial collapses, and Iriarte comes home cleared at last. Paloma's POV; exhausted vindication tinged with mourning for Ondiz and for her own lost years.

chapters.title: Shelf Life
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Paloma reopens the shop properly, filing her final case notes away — then finds one last envelope, postmarked tomorrow. Her POV; the beat is wary peace with an open door, memory proving it never truly closes.
